title: Count Reversed Two-Letter Word Pairs
description:
# Count Reversed Two-Letter Word Pairs

You are given an array `words` where every word has exactly two lowercase English letters. Count the number of index pairs `(i, j)` such that `i < j` and `words[i]` is exactly the reverse of `words[j]`.

A word may participate in more than one counted pair if there are multiple valid indices. For example, two copies of `"ab"` and two copies of `"ba"` form four index pairs. A palindromic word such as `"aa"` can pair only with another occurrence of the same word.

## Example 1:

**Input:** words = ["cd","ac","dc","ca","zz"]
**Output:** 2
**Explanation:** `"cd"` pairs with `"dc"`, and `"ac"` pairs with `"ca"`. The single `"zz"` has no later or earlier second copy.

## Example 2:

**Input:** words = ["ab","ba","ab","ba"]
**Output:** 4
**Explanation:** Each `"ab"` index can be paired with each `"ba"` index that appears on the other side of the pair ordering.

## Constraints:

*   `0 <= words.length <= 2000`
*   `words[i].length == 2`
*   `words[i]` contains only lowercase English letters.
*   Count every valid index pair; do not greedily match each word at most once.

solutions.name: Fixed Alphabet Matrix Counts
solutions.description:
## Approach

Scan the array from left to right. Store how many times each two-letter word has already appeared in a `26 x 26` matrix. For a current word `ab`, every earlier `ba` creates one valid pair, so add `seen[b][a]` before recording `ab`.

## Key Insight

The order condition `i < j` is handled by looking only at words already seen. Palindromic words also work naturally because `aa` looks up the same matrix cell before incrementing it.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1), because the matrix has only 676 cells.

solutions.name: Hash Map Reverse Lookup
solutions.description:
## Approach

Keep a frequency map of words that have appeared earlier. For each current word, construct its reverse, add the previous frequency of that reverse, then increase the frequency of the current word.

## Key Insight

Counting previous reverses avoids any need to remove or greedily match words. If there are duplicates, every earlier reverse occurrence contributes one distinct index pair.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1) under the fixed two-lowercase-letter alphabet, or O(k) for `k` distinct words.

solutions.name: Canonical Batch Aggregation
solutions.description:
## Approach

First count every two-letter word in a matrix. Then aggregate unordered reversal classes: for different letters `a` and `b`, add `count[a][b] * count[b][a]`; for palindromic words `aa`, add `k * (k - 1) / 2`.

## Key Insight

The one-pass method counts pairs online, while this route counts whole reversal groups after the scan. The formulas make the duplicate behavior explicit and prevent double counting non-palindromic classes.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n + 676)
- Space Complexity: O(1).

solutions.name: Definition Pair Enumeration
solutions.description:
## Approach

Enumerate every pair of indices `i < j` and compare the two characters directly in reversed order. Increase the answer only when `words[i][0] == words[j][1]` and `words[i][1] == words[j][0]`.

## Key Insight

This baseline mirrors the statement exactly. It is slower, but it is useful for validating optimized counting solutions on small inputs and for understanding why duplicates produce multiple pairs.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n^2)
- Space Complexity: O(1).
